title: Scaffold criteria from the chosen harness's catalog template

facts.note: Task text or a criterion's harness field naming one of the 13 catalog harnesses, or asking for a scaffold/typical layers, is matchable now.
Drafting, revising, or looking up a scaffold/layers; no existing criteria file is required (pre-file scaffold generation counts).

values: needs harness scaffold or typical layers
facts.note: Whether the planner actually needs a catalog scaffold or the harness's typical layers is judged from intent; no planning-phase observer is required.

fires: Planner drafts a new criterion with harness: http before any acceptance file exists and needs its given/when/then scaffold.
Planner looks up the catalog to see which layers a db harness typically exercises.
Planner revises a criterion's harness from unit to e2e and must re-scaffold given/when/then.
Tooling generates a criterion skeleton for a chosen harness from the catalog.
doesNotFire: Coder implementing production code against an already-authored acceptance.
Editing prose docs that neither use a harness scaffold nor need a harness's typical layers.
Choosing the harness code itself (governed by the acceptance harness vocabulary convention, not this template catalog).

given: You need a given/when/then scaffold, or the typical layers, for a criterion using one of the 13 catalog harnesses (http, unit, event, ws, e2e, a11y, visual, metric, job, db, sec, load, script) — drafting before any file exists, revising, or just looking it up.
when: You draft, generate, revise, or look up that criterion's scaffold or layers.
then: Start from the catalog entry harness -> {layers, given/when/then scaffold} (verbatim, listed in prefer), replacing its placeholder values with the criterion's real ones.
prefer: http — layers [presentation, application, domain, integration]; given {auth: {scopes: [purchase:create]}}; when {method: POST, path: /api/example, headers: {Content-Type: application/json}, body: {sample: true}}; then [{kind: status, expect: 200}, {kind: body, expect: {ok: true}}].
unit — layers [application, domain]; when {target: Service.method, args: {payload: {sample: true}}}; then [{kind: result, expect: {ok: true}}].
event — layers [application, integration]; when {topic: sample.event, payload: {sample: true}}; then [{kind: event, expect: sample.event}] (expect names the same topic).
ws — layers [integration]; when {url: ws://example/events, subscribe_msg: {action: subscribe, channel: updates}}; then [{kind: message, expect: {frame: connected}}].
e2e — layers [presentation, application, domain, integration]; when {url: http://example/ui, actions: ['fill #field', 'click #submit']}; then [{kind: visual, expect: success-banner}].
a11y — layers [presentation]; when {}; then [{kind: a11y, expect: passes}].
visual — layers [presentation]; when {}; then [{kind: snapshot, expect: unchanged}].
metric — layers [application, integration]; when {}; then [{kind: metric, expect: metric:placeholder}].
job — layers [application, integration]; when {}; then [{kind: status, expect: completed}].
db — layers [integration, domain]; when {}; then [{kind: rows, expect: updated}].
sec — layers [application, integration]; when {}; then [{kind: security, expect: granted}].
load — layers [integration, application]; when {}; then [{kind: metrics, expect: within_limits}].
script — layers [application]; when {}; then [{kind: status, expect: 0}].
Treat each template's layers as the layers the harness typically exercises — a default, not a mandatory declaration.
avoid: Leaving template placeholder values (/api/example, sample: true, Service.method, example URLs, metric:placeholder) in a finished criterion.
Inventing an ad-hoc given/when/then shape for a harness that already has a catalog template.
why: A reusable scaffold per harness keeps criteria uniform and records which layers each harness typically exercises.
evidence: Each criterion's given/when/then uses the key shape of its harness's catalog template (prefer[0..12]).
Any layers stated for a criterion are consistent with the harness's typical layers in the catalog.
verifier_detail: Catalog term harness_template ('Harness templates'): harness -> {layers, given/when/then scaffold} (verbatim). 13 harness templates: http, unit, event, ws, e2e, a11y, visual, metric, job, db, sec, load, script.

Full catalog values are in prefer[0..12]; compare criterion key shapes (given/when/then kinds) against them. Harnesses a11y, visual, metric, job, db, sec, load, script have an empty when {} in the template; only http has a given block (auth.scopes).
audit: Original name: 'Harness scaffolding templates'; statement: 'Reusable given/when/then scaffolding template per harness, with the layers it typically exercises.'

additions.text: replacing its placeholder values with the criterion's real ones
additions.justification: Source templates use placeholder values (/api/example, sample: true, metric:placeholder); 'scaffolding template' implies they are to be filled in, and stating it prevents placeholders leaking into real criteria.

additions.text: Leaving template placeholders in a finished criterion; inventing ad-hoc shapes when a template exists.
additions.justification: Concrete anti-patterns derived from the source's 'reusable scaffolding' intent; source has no explicit avoid list.
Source gives the catalog but no verification statement; these describe how compliance against the catalog is established.

Required by schema; derived from graph context (criteria shape selects a template; acceptance harness vocabulary owns the harness set). Deliberately not gated on phase, existing files, or layer declaration.

additions.text: Coder-facing text exceeds ~1,000/1,200 chars because all 13 templates are reproduced verbatim in prefer.
additions.justification: Auditor required the full scaffold catalog to be author-facing reference content; losslessness wins over brevity.
